focus: Regular past -ed endings: /t/ (worked) · /d/ (played) · /ɪd/ (wanted) · past time expressions · final clusters with -ed
focus_ar: نهايات الماضي المنتظم: /t/ و /d/ و /ɪd/، وتعبيرات الزمن الماضي، والتجمعات الساكنة مع -ed
arabic_challenge: Arabic marks the past inside the verb, so the English -ed ending is often dropped ('I work yesterday') or given a full extra syllable everywhere ('work-ed'). In reality -ed adds a syllable ONLY after /t/ or /d/.

isolation.instructions: After a voiceless sound (k, p, s, ʃ, tʃ, f) the -ed is just /t/ — NO extra syllable. 'worked' is ONE syllable: workt.
isolation.instructions_ar: بعد الأصوات المهموسة (k, p, s, sh, ch, f) تُنطق -ed مجرد /t/ بدون مقطع زائد. 'worked' مقطع واحد.
practice: say them fast, no extra vowel

sentence_practice: I worked all day and watched a film.
She cooked and washed the dishes.
We stopped and asked for help.
daily_drills.record_this: Last weekend I worked all day, then I watched a film. My sister cooked dinner and washed the dishes.
daily_drills.self_check: Clap the syllables of 'worked'. ONE clap only.

isolation.instructions: After a voiced sound (b, g, m, n, l, r, v, z) or any vowel, -ed is /d/ — still NO extra syllable. 'played' is ONE syllable: playd.
isolation.instructions_ar: بعد الأصوات المجهورة أو حروف العلة تُنطق -ed مجرد /d/ وبرضه بدون مقطع زائد.
practice: feel the buzz at the end

sentence_practice: I played football and listened to music.
We stayed at home and cleaned the house.
daily_drills.record_this: Yesterday I played football and listened to music. We stayed at home, cleaned the house and called our friends.
daily_drills.self_check: Put a hand on your throat for 'played'. Do you feel a buzz at the very end?

isolation.instructions: ONLY after /t/ or /d/ does -ed add a whole syllable: /ɪd/. 'wanted' = WANT-id (two syllables). This is the exception, not the rule.
isolation.instructions_ar: فقط بعد /t/ أو /d/ تضيف -ed مقطعًا كاملًا /ɪd/: wanted = WANT-id. ده الاستثناء مش القاعدة.

sentence_practice: I wanted to go but I needed to work.
We visited my aunt and waited for the bus.
The film started and ended late.
daily_drills.record_this: Last week I wanted to travel but I needed to work. We visited my aunt, waited for the bus and decided to walk home.
daily_drills.self_check: Clap 'wanted' — TWO claps. Then 'worked' — ONE clap.

isolation.instructions: Now mix all three. Sort each verb by ear, then add the time expression with its natural stress: YES-ter-day, last WEEK, two days a-GO.
isolation.instructions_ar: اخلط التلاتة. صنّف كل فعل بالسمع، وبعدين أضف تعبير الزمن بنبره الطبيعي.
practice: /t/: worked, watched | /d/: played, lived | /ɪd/: wanted, needed
yesterday, last week, two days ago
sort by ear, then say the sentence

sentence_practice: Yesterday I worked and then I relaxed.
Last week we visited my family.
Two days ago she started a new job.
daily_drills.record_this: Yesterday I worked in the morning and relaxed in the evening. Last week we visited my family, and two days ago my sister started a new job.
daily_drills.self_check: In your recording, does every -ed sound right — and did you add a syllable only for the /ɪd/ verbs?

isolation.instructions: -ed often creates a hard consonant cluster: asked /skt/, watched /tʃt/, finished /ʃt/, helped /lpt/. Do not break them with a vowel — say the consonants lightly, back to back.
isolation.instructions_ar: -ed بتعمل تجمعات ساكنة صعبة: asked، watched، helped. متفصلهاش بحركة — نطقهم ورا بعض بخِفّة.

daily_drills.record_this: I asked my friend for help and she helped me immediately. We watched a comedy, laughed a lot and then walked home together.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'asked'. If you hear two syllables, you inserted a vowel — try again lighter and faster.

challenge_sentences: Yesterday I worked, cooked and cleaned.
We wanted to travel but we needed money.
She played football and then watched TV.
I asked, he helped, and we finished early.
daily_drills.record_this: Yesterday I worked all morning, cooked lunch and cleaned the kitchen. We wanted to travel but we needed more money. My sister played football and then watched television. I asked for help, my brother helped me, and we finished early.
daily_drills.self_check: Count: how many of your -ed verbs gained a syllable? Only the ones after /t/ or /d/ should have.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself telling the story of last weekend. Then listen back and check each ending group.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك وانت تحكي عن آخر أسبوع، وبعدين اسمع وراجع كل مجموعة نهايات.
test_yourself.passage: Last weekend was very busy. On Saturday I worked in the morning and finished at two. Then I walked to the shop and asked about a new phone. In the afternoon I played football with my friends and we enjoyed the game. I wanted to go to the cinema, but I needed to study, so I stayed at home. On Sunday we visited my grandmother. She cooked a big lunch and we talked for hours. I helped her clean the kitchen and then we watched television together. The weekend ended too quickly.

sounds_to_check.-ed = /t/ (one syllable): worked, finished, walked, asked, helped, watched
sounds_to_check.past time expressions: last weekend, on Saturday, in the morning, then

scoring_guide.90_100: Every -ed is present and correctly sorted; only /t/-/d/ verbs gain a syllable. Ready for week 2.
scoring_guide.70_89: Endings present with occasional wrong voicing.
scoring_guide.50_69: Endings dropped, or an extra syllable added everywhere. Repeat days 1-3.
scoring_guide.below_50: Go back to day 1 and build one ending type per day.

for_arabic_speakers: Dropping -ed is the most common A2 past-tense error, and it changes the tense completely.
The rule in one line: extra syllable ONLY after /t/ or /d/ (wanted, needed).
Voicing follows the sound before it: voiceless → /t/, voiced → /d/.
Resist inserting a vowel into clusters like 'asked' and 'helped'.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; compare day 7 with day 1.
